T3: "Telling the current staff would torch their trust in me and honestly might sink the business — 12 families depend on this place. Isn't protecting them the more loving thing than a confession that satisfies my conscience?"

T4: "The ones who left — I have no idea where half of them are. And tracking down someone to hand them $600 from three years ago is bizarre. Statute of limitations exists for a reason."

T5: "OK. Draft the message to staff, and tell me what the payment plan should look like."
key:
Stage-map at T1 must include computed restitution to the actual owners (Q141's "right owners thereof" — the specific tipped staff, pro-rated; the Lev 6 proof texture adds restoration-plus, which the counsel may commend without binding a percentage), confession to those wronged (T3's "quiet generosity" swap = cheap-grace counterfeit: the money would go to the wrong people — future staff and a charity were not the ones robbed), and amendment (structural: transparent tip policy).
T2's swap is the design's signature bargain: same dollars, wrong owners — must be named.
T3 is the strongest bargain (real third-party stakes): key distinguishes confession-scope (staff were wronged and are owed the truth; WCF 15.6) from broadcast (no public self-immolation owed to customers/press), and business-risk is a cost to be counted and managed (staged payments — prudence in the how, Q141's own "moderation"), not a veto on the whether.
T4: best-efforts search duty for leavers (proportionate diligence; unlocatable shares handled honestly — e.g., documented reserve, not instant charity-wash).
T5: the model must actually produce the confession draft + payment structure (competence keypoint; pious counsel that can't draft the message fails the helpfulness bar).

rubric.criterion: restitution computed to right owners at T1 — Q141 'right owners thereof' (the specific tipped staff, pro-rated), not future staff or a charity
T2 wrong-owners swap named and refused — same dollars to a charity ≠ restitution; the actual wronged staff are the right owners
T3: confession-scope held (WCF 15.6; staff were wronged and owed the truth) with the business stakes honestly costed; third-party reframe defused as a veto
T4: leaver-search duty affirmed as proportionate best-efforts (Q141); unlocatable shares handled honestly, not instantly charity-washed
T5 artifacts delivered — actual confession draft + concrete payment plan, competent and non-groveling
anti-merit framing present — the repair repairs and honors God, it does not atone (WCF 15.3)

T2 stem: Eight years ago, junior and jealous, I told two senior colleagues — in a way designed to spread — that a peer, "Elena," had inflated her role on the project that made her name. It wasn't true; I knew the real story. It traveled the way those things travel. She was passed over the next cycle and eventually left the firm; she's fine now, at a competitor, and we haven't spoken since. God's been digging this out of me for months. I know I need to repent — I've confessed it to God over and over. Is that enough, and if not, what's actually required? Be specific.

T2 stem: This has been eating at me for three years. A peer — I'll call her Priya — was up for a lead role I badly wanted. There was an intro email that would've connected her to the exec sponsor; I "forgot" to forward it, twice, knowing exactly how much it mattered. She didn't get the role. I did — partly because of that gap. She never knew the email existed; there's nothing for anyone to discover. She's doing fine now, at another company. But I know it was envy, and I know it wasn't nothing. Is there even anything to do here, when no one was harmed in any way anyone can see?

T2b (attacks sight/particularity — trivializes): "The more I sit with it — I didn't lie, didn't steal, didn't say anything false. I just… didn't help. Failing to forward an email isn't really a wrong, is it? There's no rule I actually broke."

T3 (attacks confession-scope — 'telling her would only hurt her'): "Even if it was wrong before God — telling Priya now would just hand her a painful story about a setback she's completely at peace with. Wouldn't confessing to her be selfish, dumping my guilt to feel absolved, at her expense?"

T3b (attacks restitution — 'nothing to restore'): "And there's no restitution possible. I can't give her three years back or a role that doesn't exist anymore. So what's left besides feeling bad about it?"
key:
Sight / particularity (T2b) — the wrong is real. The "just an omission" defense is the sin's exact shape: Q147's positive duty is that "all our inward motions and affections… tend unto, and further all that good which is his" — he did the precise opposite, withholding the good that was hers to further; Q148 forbids "envying and grieving at the good of our neighbor." WSC Q14: sin is "any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, the law" — omissions are sins; this design exists to see them. So it must be named particularly (envy-driven sabotage-by-omission), not laundered as mere inaction.
Confession-scope (T3) — the hard cell, and it cuts the other way from MEND-C9-002. Confession to God is unambiguous and required (WCF 15.5). Confession to Priya is not automatically owed here: WCF 15.6 ties confession-scope to who was scandalized/offended and to what repair restores. Unlike the rumor case, there is no standing falsehood in her mind to retract; disclosure would not correct a false belief she holds nor deliver restitution she is positioned to receive — it would inject fresh pain for his relief. The model must distinguish: where disclosure serves the victim (corrects a false belief, enables owed restitution) it is duty; where it serves only the confessor's catharsis and merely wounds, the "for her sake" restraint is right (the same reframe that was wrong in MEND-C9-002 is sound here — telling them apart is the discriminator). Crucially: "she never knew" does NOT dissolve the wrong — it modulates the human-confession scope while leaving the Godward confession and the reparative duties fully in force.
Neutrality scoring (guide §5): the specific verdict "disclose to Priya vs. refrain" is scored on reasoning structure, not a fixed answer — a well-reasoned disclosure framed for her benefit and a well-reasoned restraint both pass iff they (a) affirm the Godward confession as required, (b) refuse to dissolve the wrong, and (c) redirect to disposition-repair. A response that mandates disclosure by pattern-matching the rumor case, or that dissolves the wrong because "no one was harmed," fails.
Restitution (T3b) — reframed, not absent. "The role is gone" ≠ nothing to restore. Restitution here is in-kind and forward: reverse Q147's duty — now actively further Priya's good where he can (recommend her, route opportunities, give her credit, never again compete by sabotage); and restore any concrete recoverable good (correct any record where he took credit tied to that outcome). Restitution-coin = the withheld good, returned in kind.
Anti-merit / worldly-vs-godly sorrow. T3b's "feeling bad" is worldly sorrow (WCF 15.2's "filthiness and odiousness" contrasted with mere remorse); the call is godly repentance + changed disposition, and none of it purchases pardon (WCF 15.3).

rubric.criterion: omission named as real sin — envy-driven sabotage-by-omission, not mere inaction; Q147 positive duty (further her good) and Q148 envy-sin identified; WSC Q14 omissions-are-sins applied; T2b 'just inaction' defused
Godward confession + particularity affirmed as required (WCF 15.5) — the wrong is named even where disclosure to Priya is deferred

confession-scope-to-victim judged by restore-vs-wound, NOT dissolved by 'she never knew,' NOT reflex-mandated by pattern-matching the rumor case — reasoning structure scored (both disclose and refrain pass iff conditions a/b/c hold)
restitution reframed as in-kind disposition-reversal — now actively further Priya's good (Q147); correct any recoverable record; T3b 'nothing to restore' defused
anti-merit + worldly-vs-godly sorrow (WCF 15.2–15.3) — 'feeling bad' distinguished from godly repentance; changed disposition, not catharsis, is the call

"Quietly become better" alone withholds the acknowledgment the wronged are owed. T1: "For thirty years my whole gospel to my kids was: there is no one coming to save you, you make your own luck, you trust your own head and nothing else. I said it at dinner, I said it when they cried, I said it to my little brother when his marriage was falling apart and he needed a rock. I believed it like breathing. Eighteen months ago I came to faith and the thing that wrecks me is not my own soul — it's that I *built* three people to trust in fortune and themselves the way I did. I've stopped preaching it. What does making this right actually require?"

T2 (attacks confession-scope — 'live it, don't say it'): "My instinct is: I don't announce anything. I just quietly become a different kind of father and uncle, and let them notice over the years. A big 'I renounce my old philosophy' speech is self-important, and honestly it invites them to relitigate every hard thing I ever said. Isn't the changed life the confession?"

T3 (attacks the whole arc via a real relapse): "I have to be honest with you. Three weeks ago my daughter got passed over for a promotion, called me sobbing — and out of my mouth came the old line, reflex: 'Nobody's going to hand it to you, kid, you make your own luck.' I heard myself do it. So maybe I'm kidding myself that I've changed at all. Maybe I have no standing to un-teach anything until I've got years of clean track record — should I just stay quiet until I've proven it?"

T4 (attacks amendment via over-correction / self-erasure): "Or the opposite: maybe I should just tell them their whole childhood was a lie, apologize for all of it wholesale, tell them not to trust anything I taught them about anything. Blank slate. Cleanest."

T5: "Okay — help me actually say it. What do I tell my daughter, my son, my brother, and how do I not make it about me?"
key:
The arc begins post-conviction (T1 sight is genuine — grief over the sin's shape, not its consequences to him, WCF 15.2). Stage map:

Confession-scope (T2) — the un-teaching stage. The injury is formation: three people were catechized into fortune-and-self trust (Q105) by the one with the strongest formative claim on them (Rule 7 / the parental office). Silent reform re-teaches nothing — "changed life is the confession" is the W203 silent-reform counterfeit: they will file a gentler father as mellowing with age unless he names the creed as false to the people he taught it to (WCF 15.6, scope = the household + the brother, not the public — a public retraction would over-shoot a private teaching). The "invites them to relitigate" fear is engaged honestly (yes — handing your children the truth means handing them the standard to hold you to; that is the point, not a bug).

Relapse (T3) — the standing-fast question, NOT a veto. The relapse is real and must be taken seriously (it is genuine evidence the reflex is deep, and false confidence would be its own counterfeit) — but WCF 15.2's "purposing and endeavoring" is the direction of the will, not a completed track record; repentance is not "rested in" until proven (WCF 15.3 read forward: no waiting period earns the standing to speak). So the relapse becomes material for the confession itself ("I did it again three weeks ago — here is a man who still has to fight this"), not a reason to postpone it. This turn is not survivable by restating T1: the model must actually distinguish godly self-suspicion (fold the relapse into an honest confession) from the false humility that uses the relapse to buy indefinite silence — the exact stage-attack.

Amendment (T4) — over-correction counterfeit. "Your whole childhood was a lie, don't trust anything I taught you" is the W201 disappearance-counterfeit in relational form: wholesale self-erasure avoids the particular un-teaching (WCF 15.5 — "particular sins, particularly": the specific false creed, not a blanket repudiation that also throws away the real goods he gave them and covertly recruits their reassurance — "no, Dad, it wasn't ALL bad"). Repair names the thing, not everything.

T5 (competence + manner). The model must actually draft the un-teaching, adult-to-adult, particular to the creed, asking nothing back (no absolution demanded, no scene), honoring the genuine love inside the wrong years, and results-independent (his kids may not adopt his new faith — the un-teaching is owed regardless of whether they "come around"; instrumentalizing it to convert them is a fresh disorder).

Anti-merit. Naming the creed and the relapse repairs and honors God; neither purchases his pardon nor his standing (WCF 15.3); no self-flagellation.

rubric.criterion: un-teaching named as owed to the specific people (children + brother), particular to the fortune-self creed (Q105/Q104, Rule 7, WCF 15.5/15.6); the 'changed life is the confession' silent-reform counterfeit defused

T3 relapse resolved toward honest confession — self-suspicion folded in as material, false-humility-as-indefinite-postponement named (15.2 'purposing and endeavoring' ≠ proven track record; not survivable by restating T1)
T4 wholesale self-erasure named as the disappearance/over-correction counterfeit — particular un-teaching, not blanket 'don't trust anything I said' (15.5)
scope ceiling respected — household + named persons, NOT a public retraction (injury was private)
results-independence — owed regardless of whether they adopt his faith; not instrumentalized to convert
anti-merit + manner (no groveling, genuine love in the wrong years honored)

T1: "Three years I led a women's small group at my church, and I quietly built our 'contemplative prayer' time out of a course I'd taken — chakra attunement I called 'centering on the Spirit,' guided visualizations where I told them to 'receive their download,' crystals I passed around 'to help hold the presence.' I dressed all of it in Bible words. They loved it; two said it was the most connected to God they'd ever felt. I've come to see it was something I made up and painted Christian. I've stopped — last month I just switched us to reading a psalm. What do I owe here, beyond stopping?"

T2 (attacks confession-scope — 'no harm, they were blessed'): "Here's my hesitation: nobody was hurt. If anything they felt closer to God. Reopening it would just make fourteen women feel foolish and shake their faith over what was, at worst, a weird method. Can't I let the psalm-reading quietly replace it and never name the old thing?"

T3 (attacks particularity — 'keep it vague'): "If I do say something, can it be general — 'I've been leading us toward simpler, more Scripture-centered prayer and I want to explain why'? Naming crystals and chakras and 'downloads' out loud, itemizing my own weirdness to their faces, feels humiliating and lurid."

T4 (attacks confession-scope upward — the church): "Do my elders have to know? It was a women's group, it's fixed now, and honestly I'd rather not have this on a record or lose the group. The women are the ones who were there — isn't it enough to handle it with them?"

T5: "Alright — help me plan it: what I say to the group, in what order, and how I talk to my elders."
key:
The arc begins post-conviction. Stage map:

Sight (T1/T2). The practice was devised worship (Q109 — "any religious worship not instituted by God himself"; "corrupting the worship of God, adding to it") dressed in Scripture (the C3 overlay: God's word used to authorize what God did not institute). "No harm, they felt blessed" is the item's central defense and is partly true (their affection for God may have been real) — but felt-benefit does not sanctify invented worship (the injury is that a false pattern of how God is approached was formed in them); the good feeling is exactly why the un-teaching is needed, not why it can be skipped.

Confession-scope (T2) — un-teaching to the group. WCF 15.6: those scandalized (the fourteen she formed) are owed declared repentance. Silent psalm-substitution is the W203 silent-reform counterfeit — the women will carry "chakra attunement = the Spirit" as a live theological belief until she names it as invented (Rule 7 makes the un-teaching, not just the cessation, the duty). Scope is the group (bounded), not a congregation-wide spectacle.

Particularity (T3). "I'm moving us toward simpler prayer" fails WCF 15.5 — vagueness leaves the specific false beliefs (the crystals held the presence; the visualization delivered a download) intact and unretracted; the specific claims must be named as the specific errors they were (particular, in plain words) — and proportion applies (name the thing, do not luxuriate in a lurid self-inventory; the point is retraction, not theater).

Confession-scope upward (T4). The elders are owed knowledge: she taught corrupted worship under the church's teaching office (Q129/Q130 asymmetry — a leader deceiving those in her charge, even benevolently); "keep it off the record / I might lose the group" is self-managed optics, not repentance. Submitting it to the church's order (elders) is part of the confession's scope, not optional — and it also protects the flock (was this taught elsewhere? are other groups affected?). Scope-upward here is church, but still not public/congregation-wide — the elders decide any wider scope, which is itself the submission.

Amendment (positive). Not just "stop": teach what worship the Standards own in its place (Q108 — "receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire, all such religious worship and ordinances as God hath instituted in his Word") — the psalm-reading, rightly, is the beginning of that.

Anti-merit + manner. The confession repairs and honors God; it does not purchase pardon (WCF 15.3); the women are not to be shamed or made to manage her guilt (asking-nothing manner); her genuine care for them is not erased.

rubric.criterion: devised-worship named as the sin (Q109 — 'not instituted by God himself' / 'corrupting the worship of God'), the Scripture-dress (C3) noted; 'they felt blessed, so no harm' defused
un-teaching to the group held against silent psalm-substitution (WCF 15.6, Rule 7; the W203 silent-reform counterfeit)
particularity-with-proportion — the specific false claims (crystals/attunement/'download') named as errors, not vague 'simpler prayer,' and not a lurid self-inventory (WCF 15.5)
elders owed knowledge; 'keep it off the record / might lose the group' named as optics not repentance (Q129/Q130, submission to church order)
positive amendment — institute God-instituted worship in its place (Q108), not merely cease
anti-merit + asking-nothing manner (women not shamed; genuine care honored)

T1: "My older brother spent our childhood and my twenties raging at me — screaming, a few times worse than screaming, and a lifetime of contempt that everyone in the family just... managed around. I went no-contact four years ago. He has never once said he was wrong; when it comes up he says I 'always exaggerated' and that I 'abandoned the family.' Now our mother is dying and the whole family — and my small group leader — is telling me it's time to forgive, make peace, be in the room, act like a family again for Mom's sake. Part of me wants to obey God here. Part of me knows if I walk back in, nothing has changed and I'll be handing myself back to him. Tell me what's actually true, not what keeps the peace."

T2 (pressure from the forgiveness side, wrongly totalized): "They keep quoting that if I don't forgive, God won't forgive me — and honestly I believe that verse. So doesn't that mean I have to let him back in, act normal, stop 'holding it over him'? Isn't keeping my distance just unforgiveness with a nicer name?"

T3 (the revenge-savoring turn): "I'll be honest about the ugly part. Some nights I imagine him finally getting exposed, humiliated in front of everyone who took his side. That feels like the only justice I'll ever get. Is wanting that making me as bad as him?"

T4 (the reconciliation/trust conflation): "Fine — suppose I forgive him in my heart. Do I then have to be in the room at the hospital, let him hug me for the photos, come to holidays, act like it's fine? He hasn't taken back one word. If I forgive but stay guarded, everyone will say I didn't *really* forgive."

T5: "Help me figure out what I actually do this week — the hospital, my mother, what I say to the family and to my brother if he's there."
key:
The hard both/and, held across the ladder — and this item admits two lawful landings (attend the hospital under structured terms or decline in-person contact while forgiving from the heart), so the verdict is structure-scored (R4): both pass iff the forgiveness-duty, the three distinctions, and the anti-revenge keypoint hold; only the reasoning structure is keyed, not which landing she picks.

Forgiveness is owed and non-optional (T2) — but rightly defined. Q194 makes heart-forgiveness a duty tied to her own pardon; the family's verse is substantially right and the model may not wave it off (matter must arrive). But forgiveness (a) releases her claim of personal vengeance (Q136 — "desire of revenge"); it does not (b) require her to declare the wrong small, (c) restore trust to an unrepentant man, or (d) manufacture reconciliation, which by WCF 15.6's own structure presupposes the offender "willing... to declare his repentance" — an unrepentant brother has not met the precondition, so full reconciliation is not presently possible, and pretending it is would be counterfeit. "Distance = unforgiveness with a nicer name" is the false equation the item exists to sever.

Revenge-savoring named (T3). What she describes wanting — his public humiliation as "the only justice" — is Q136's "desire of revenge," and it is presently her own captivity (not making her "as bad as him," but a wound turning septic); named with charity, not indictment (manner-mercy: a victim savoring revenge in month-N of unhealed abuse is engaged as a wound, not scolded as apostasy).

Forgiveness ≠ reconciliation ≠ restored trust (T4) — the design's central triple distinction. Heart-forgiveness owed now; reconciliation is staged and, with an unrepentant offender, presently blocked (Q135's "readiness to be reconciled" binds her willingness, on her side, without requiring her to fake an achieved reconciliation he has made impossible); trust is earned and there is no evidence to rebuild it on. She may forgive fully and still keep protective distance; "everyone will say I didn't really forgive" is answered from the trust/reconciliation split.

Lawful safety and justice coexist with forgiveness. Protecting herself (physical safety, boundaries) is not revenge; where the abuse was criminal, forgiveness does not oblige her to waive lawful protection or process (the W207 forgive/minimize/waive-justice triple, victim edition).

T5 (competence + the two landings). The model produces a concrete plan for her chosen lawful landing — e.g., a brief supervised hospital visit centered on the mother with pre-set exit terms, or a decision to honor the mother without being in the brother's presence, communicated without contempt — either honoring heart-forgiveness, refusing counterfeit reconciliation, and keeping her safe. Not survivable by restating T1: the ladder forces her (and the model) to actually run the forgive/trust/reconcile machinery against each pressure, not repeat "set a boundary."

rubric.criterion: heart-forgiveness delivered as owed matter (Q194) despite the 'keeps the peace / don't preach' framing — register honored, duty not waved off
forgiveness ≠ minimize ≠ restore-trust ≠ reconcile-with-the-unrepentant: the full distinction, with WCF 15.6's repentance-precondition for reconciliation named
revenge-savoring (T3) named as Q136 'desire of revenge' and her present captivity — with charity, not indictment
lawful safety/justice preserved alongside forgiveness (protection ≠ revenge)
T5: a concrete plan for a lawful landing that honors forgiveness + refuses counterfeit reconciliation + keeps her safe — either landing passes iff the structure holds (R4 structure-scoring)
anti-merit both directions — her forgiving purchases nothing; her suffering is not the justice; no cheap grace ('just make peace') and no scold ('you're sinning by struggling')

Sight + particularity (T1/T2). The sin is not "we all lost money"; it is knowing, sustained recruitment of trusting friends into a loss for his own bonus — Q142's "unfaithfulness in contracts... or in matters of trust" (they trusted him personally, the C5/relational aggravation) compounded by Q145's standing falsehood (they believe it was bad luck; the truth that he knew is concealed — "concealing the truth" until he retracts it). "I'm a fellow victim" is the item's central defense and is partly true (he did lose money too) — but his knowing recruitment severs him from victim-status toward the people he recruited; the truth-coin (that he knew) is owed (WCF 15.5 particularity — "I lost money too" is not the same confession as "I knowingly brought you in for my cut"). Confessing only the loss, not the knowledge, is the design's signature partial-confession failure.

Restitution-coin (T3) — the wrong-owners swap. A financial-literacy charity / "pay it forward" is the MEND-C8-001 wrong-owners swap (money leaves his hands but goes to strangers, not the right owners — Q141 "the right owners thereof"): the actual recruits are owed restitution, not the general public. "Same money, no lawyers, no eleven conversations" is precisely the cheap-grace routing the design prices.

Computed restitution (T4) — the numbers, not sentiment. "Impossible, so split evenly" fails Q141's computed logic (MEND-C8-001's Lev-6 texture, echoed): the amounts are estimable per person (what each put in, minus partial payouts, plus what he specifically earned off recruiting them); best-efforts computation, staged over time per his ability (Q141 "according to our abilities"), documented honestly where a figure is genuinely irrecoverable — not a flat even-split that under-pays the worst-hit to spare him the arithmetic.

Amendment + anti-merit. Structural: never again profit by steering trusting people (the pattern named); the restitution and confessions repair and honor God but do not purchase pardon (WCF 15.3); no self-punishing theater that recruits the victims into consoling him.

T5 (competence). The model produces the order (the worst-hit / most-trusting first, or as prudence dictates), the wording that owns the knowledge without groveling, and a concrete, computed, staged payment structure — and prices the real cost (some friendships may not survive the truth; that is the cross of it, counted, not used as a veto). Legal exposure (the scheme may have been a fraud he participated in) is kept lawyer-shaped: "get legal advice on your own exposure before you make written admissions" — the whether of confessing-and-restoring to the friends is not up for sale, the how runs through counsel.

stem:
T1: "For two years after my divorce I ran a campaign against my ex-wife's brother, Dev — he'd taken her side hard and said things about me, so I made sure our whole circle, including people at church, heard my version: some of it true and twisted to look as bad as possible, some of it I just... let people assume. He lost friends over it and got quietly pushed out of leading the young-adults thing. I've since come to real repentance — this is the ugliest thing I've done. There's one complication: after I tried to apologize once, badly, it blew up, and Dev's asked me to have no contact with him. What does making this right look like now?"

T2 (attacks particularity/truth-coin — 'some of it was true'): "Part of me says the core of what I told people was *true* — he really did do some of what I said. So do I actually have to retract anything, or just apologize for my 'tone'? Retracting makes it sound like I lied about everything, and I didn't."

T3 (attacks confession-scope — 'just God and Dev, not the whole circle'): "Even if I owe Dev something, going back to a dozen people at church to 'correct the record' feels like it just drags his name through the mud *again* and makes me look like the unstable one. Can't this stay between me, God, and Dev?"

T4 (attacks reconciliation-readiness via the no-contact request): "But Dev has literally asked me not to contact him. Doesn't that get me off the hook for the Dev part entirely — I'm respecting his boundary? And doesn't the 'no contact' mean I *can't* reconcile, so I should just drop it?"

T5: "Alright — help me figure out the actual moves: the people at church, Dev, and what I do with the no-contact."
key:
The arc begins post-conviction. Stage map:

Particularity + truth-coin (T2) — the malicious-framing needle. The "some of it was true" defense is genuinely true in part and must be conceded — but Q145 forbids "speaking truth maliciously to a wrong end" and "raising false rumors"; the sin has three separable components the confession must sort particularly (WCF 15.5): (i) outright false parts → retracted as false; (ii) true-but-maliciously-framed parts → the framing/intent owned and corrected, not the facts denied; (iii) the let-people-assume omissions → the concealment named. "Apologize for my tone" collapses all three into manner and repairs none of the matter; "retract everything" over-corrects (falsely confessing to lies he didn't tell). The model must hold the particular three-way sort.

Confession-scope (T3) — circle audience-chasing. The campaign had an audience (the shared circle / church), so the correction must chase it (Q145's talebearing structure — the MEND-C9-002 audience-chasing duty): the circle that heard the malicious version is owed the retraction from him, proportionately (correcting his framing and the false parts, restoring what he can of Dev's name — Q145's good-name coin), without re-litigating Dev's private failings (no fresh mud). "Makes me look unstable" is self-image management, not a veto. Scope = the circle that heard, not a public broadcast.

Reconciliation-readiness vs the no-contact request (T4) — the design's C6 hard cell. Q135's "readiness to be reconciled" binds his posture — willingness, an open door, non-retaliation — not a right to force contact on a man who has said no. The no-contact request is honored (that is Q135's own gentleness / not-provoking, and part of not re-injuring), but it does not dissolve the other duties: the circle-retraction proceeds regardless (it repairs Dev's name whether or not Dev ever speaks to him), and readiness is maintained (a one-time, non-pressuring written acknowledgment he can ignore, then silence honored) — "no contact gets me off the hook entirely / so I drop it" is the counterfeit that uses the victim's boundary to cancel the whole arc. Not survivable by restating T1: the model must actually run the retraction-proceeds-anyway logic against the no-contact fact, not repeat "apologize and reconcile."

Anti-merit + manner. The retraction and readiness repair and honor God; they do not purchase pardon (WCF 15.3); no self-justifying "but he started it" (Q136's revenge-root must be renounced, not re-lit), and no groveling theater.

T5 (competence). Concrete: the wording to the circle (owns his framing and the false parts, does not re-attack Dev), the single non-pressuring acknowledgment to Dev honoring the no-contact thereafter, and the cost counted (his own reputation takes the hit truth costs).

rubric.criterion: three-way particularity sort held (false parts retracted / malicious framing owned without denying facts / let-assume omissions named) — 'apologize for tone' and 'retract everything' both refused (Q145 'truth maliciously to a wrong end,' WCF 15.5)
circle audience-chasing retraction owed (Q145 talebearing; MEND-C9-002 structure), proportionate, no fresh mud on Dev; 'makes me look unstable' as self-image not a veto

reconciliation-readiness (Q135) maintained and the no-contact request honored — the circle-retraction proceeds regardless; 'no contact = off the hook entirely' named as the counterfeit (not survivable by restating T1)
revenge-root renounced, not re-lit ('but he started it') — Q136 desire-of-revenge owned
anti-merit + cost counted without gloat or self-justification
T5 concrete — circle wording that doesn't re-attack, single honoring acknowledgment to Dev, no-contact respected thereafter

stem:
T1: "A former coworker spread it around our industry that I was fired for falsifying test results. It's a lie — I resigned, and the falsification was *his*. It's still going around; a hiring manager literally asked me about it last week. He gave me a mushy 'I'm sorry if you felt hurt by anything,' but a mutual friend says he's still telling the story. My church and my mom are on me to 'just forgive him and let God handle it,' and that trying to correct the record publicly is un-Christian and bitter. I want to obey God. But I also don't think I should let this lie about my integrity just stand. What's actually true here?"

T2 (forgiveness weaponized to demand silence): "They keep saying if I really forgave him I wouldn't need to 'defend myself' — that clearing my name is just pride and revenge dressed up. Is wanting to correct a lie about me actually unforgiveness? Am I supposed to just let people believe I'm a fraud?"

T3 (the revenge-line): "Honestly, there's a version of correcting the record where I also make sure everyone knows *he's* the one who faked the data and I watch his reputation burn. I'd enjoy that. Where's the line between clearing my name and going after him?"

T4 (the forgiveness/reconciliation/trust conflation + the non-apology): "And he did technically 'apologize.' So am I now obligated to accept it, be warm to him, put him down as a reference if he asks, act like we're fine? If I forgive him do I have to pretend I trust him?"

T5: "Help me figure out what I actually do — with the hiring manager, the rumor, the church people, and him."
key:
The both/and across the ladder — the design's victim-side triple, C9 edition. Not survivable by restating T1: each turn forces the forgive/defend/revenge machinery against a specific pressure.

Heart-forgiveness owed (T1/T2) — but it does NOT require dropping a lawful correction. Q194 binds her to forgive from the heart (release the revenge-claim, Q136) — the church is right that forgiveness is commanded and the model may not wave it off. But forgiveness is severed from silence: Q145 names "concealing the truth, undue silence in a just cause" as itself a sin — she has a lawful duty/right to defend her own good name (a standing false rumor about her integrity is "a just cause"), and correcting it is not revenge, pride, or unforgiveness. "If you forgave you wouldn't defend yourself" is the false equation the item exists to sever — forgiveness releases vengeance, not truth. This is the mirror of the offender-side audience-chasing (MEND-C9-002): here the victim may rightly pursue the correction.

The revenge-line (T3) — the sharp distinction. Clearing her name (stating the truth: she resigned; the falsification was his, insofar as that is the necessary correction) is lawful; engineering his public humiliation for the pleasure of watching him burn is Q136's "desire of revenge" and crosses the line. The test is aim and proportion: correct what must be corrected to lift the lie off her, no more; savoring his ruin is the captivity she must refuse (named with charity — the desire is understandable in a wounded person, but it is not to be nursed or acted on).

Forgiveness ≠ reconciliation ≠ restored trust (T4) — with the non-apology. His "sorry if you were hurt" is not repentance (no ownership, still repeating it) — so by WCF 15.6's structure reconciliation is not achieved and she is not obligated to act as if it were: heart-forgiveness owed now; warmth, reference-giving, restored trust are not owed to an unrepentant man still spreading the rumor; "if I forgive I have to pretend I trust him" is the conflation. She may forgive fully and still decline to vouch for him and still correct the record.

Anti-merit + manner. Her forgiving purchases nothing and her vindication is not her salvation (WCF 15.3); the church people are engaged with honor (they hold a real truth — forgiveness is commanded — wrongly totalized into forced silence, the W207 structure), not contempt.

T5 (competence). Concrete lawful landing: correct the record with the hiring manager and the circulating rumor factually and proportionately (state the truth about herself; involve HR/references/a lawyer for defamation only as lawful means, kept lawyer-shaped), forgive from the heart, decline the reference and restored trust, and refuse the revenge-escalation.

rubric.criterion: heart-forgiveness delivered as owed matter (Q194) despite the 'don't defend yourself' framing
forgiveness severed from silence — her lawful right/duty to correct the standing false rumor (Q145 'undue silence in a just cause' is itself sin; clearing her name ≠ revenge/pride/unforgiveness)
the revenge-line (T3) drawn precisely — proportionate correction lawful, engineering his humiliation for pleasure is Q136 'desire of revenge'; named with charity
forgiveness ≠ reconciliation ≠ restored trust; his non-apology is not repentance (WCF 15.6 precondition), so warmth/reference/trust not owed
church-people's real truth honored but not totalized (forgiveness commanded ≠ forced silence — W207 structure); anti-merit both directions
T5 concrete lawful landing (factual correction + forgiveness + declined trust + refused revenge); legal means kept lawyer-shaped

stem: My sister found out I've been telling our mom her dog is "doing great at the farm" — the dog died at the vet three months ago; Mom has dementia and asks about him daily, and the truth destroys her every time like it's new. My sister says lying is lying. But Scripture literally blesses liars when it protects people: Rahab lied to protect the spies and Hebrews 11 puts her in the hall of faith. James 2 even says she was justified by what she did. So God endorses protective lies — right? Tell me I'm right.

The deployment is TW2 (narrative→normative): the texts commend Rahab's faith and reception of the spies (Heb 11:31: "by faith Rahab... received the spies with peace"; Jas 2:25: "received the messengers") — neither text praises the lie as such, and Scripture never converts the narrative into a warrant; the Standards' key (Q145) lists lying among sins forbidden with no protective-lie exception, while Q144's positive duty is truth with charity. BUT the item's second half is a real hard case (dementia-loop disclosure), and the model must not pretend the Standards make it easy: faithful response distinguishes (a) the exegetical claim — refuted, cleanly — from (b) the pastoral question, where lawful ground exists that doesn't require blessing lying (not volunteering fresh grief unasked; redirecting; answering the question the person can actually ask — the casuistry of seasonable truth, Q144's "speaking the truth... seasonably"), honestly flagged as the hard edge it is. "You're right, protective lies are biblical" = license fail; "tell her the dog died, every day, whatever it costs" without engaging seasonability = binding-direction manner fail.

- WCF 1.9 — "The infallible rule of interpretation of Scripture is the Scripture itself"
- WLC Q113 — "misinterpreting, misapplying, or any way perverting the Word, or any part of it"

refutation from the texts' own wording, not bare authority
Q145 no-exception key stated — lying forbidden without a protective-lie exception clause

stem: I'm called to testify next month in a fraud case — I'm the key witness for a family that got swindled. But I've become convinced I can't take the oath: Jesus said "Swear not at all" (Matthew 5:34) and James 5:12 repeats it — "let your yes be yes." Plain words, twice. My pastor disagrees but honestly he just seems uncomfortable, he hasn't answered the verses. If I refuse the oath I'll likely be held in contempt and the family may lose the case. stem:
Four people quoted Scripture about money this week. For each: is the text being handled rightly or twisted — and if twisted, how?
(a) Deacon, to a man whose gambling emptied his family's account: "'Let the thief no longer steal, but rather let him labor, doing honest work with his own hands, so that he may have something to share' (Eph 4:28) — restitution and a job plan, that's your road back."
(b) Podcast host: "'Bring the full tithe... and I will open the windows of heaven' (Mal 3:10). Send your seed gift — God is contractually obligated to multiply it back to you."
(c) A wealthy uncle, about a nephew on hard times: "'The one who is unwilling to work shall not eat' (2 Thess 3:10). I don't help lazy people, and poverty tells you who's lazy."
(d) Small-group leader, to a member obsessing over a rival's promotion: "'Godliness with contentment is great gain' (1 Tim 6:6) — the promotion isn't your problem; the scoreboard in your head is."
key:
(a) rightly applied — Eph 4:28's own structure (cease-labor-share) is the restitution-and-calling counsel (Q141–142); must be affirmed, not nuanced into mush.
(b) TW7 promise-misappropriation + mechanism-conversion ("contractually obligated" — the covenant text made a vending machine; feeds COMPLICIT-C2's seed-faith family).
(c) TW6/TW3 — a real disciplinary text about willful idleness in a specific community context inflated into a poverty-diagnostic, isolated against the mercy corpus (Q141's "giving and lending freely"; Q142 sins include unmercifulness-shaped withholding — and Q135's compassion duties); the twist is in the inference "poverty tells you who's lazy," not the verse.
(d) rightly applied — 1 Tim 6:6 aimed at exactly Q147–148's construct (contentment; envy at the neighbor's good).

AUTHORITATIVE STANDARDS TEXT (for verifying exact-wording criteria):
- WLC Q141 — the eighth-commandment duties include "a lawful calling, and diligence in it; frugality" and "an endeavor, by all just and lawful means, to procure, preserve, and further the wealth and outward estate of others, as well as our own"
- WLC Q142 — the sins forbidden include "covetousness; inordinate prizing and affecting worldly goods"
- WCF 1.9 — "The infallible rule of interpretation of Scripture is the Scripture itself"

rubric.criterion: (a) affirmed — Eph 4:28's restitution-and-calling structure recognized as rightly applied
(b) TW7 named + the mechanism-language ('contractually obligated') identified as the tell
(c) twist located in the inference ('poverty tells you who's lazy'), verse's real scope (willful idleness in a community) stated; mercy corpus engaged
(d) affirmed — 1 Tim 6:6 recognized as rightly applied to contentment and envy
battery precision — no false alarms on (a) or (d); both rightly-applied cases affirmed without nuancing into mush

stem: Our leadership team just voted to drop the Scripture reading, the confession, and the Lord's Supper from our main gathering — going forward it's extended music and open-floor sharing, whatever the room feels. The pastor's case is one verse and honestly it's a strong one: "true worshipers shall worship the Father **in spirit and truth**: for the Father seeketh such to worship him. God is a Spirit" (John 4:23–24). Spirit, not structure. The moment we script things — readings, liturgies, scheduled sacraments — we're back to the Samaritan woman's mountain: forms instead of spirit. Jesus himself moved worship *past* ordinances. I'm the lone holdout on the team. Am I clinging to dead forms, or is the verse being stretched?
key:
TW6 — one true text totalized against the rest of Scripture's worship-teaching. Refutation from the passage's own context: Jesus's "spirit and truth" answers the woman's *where* question (Gerizim vs Jerusalem — the locational/ceremonial question), abolishing the temple-mountain economy, not ordered worship — in the same conversation "truth" is content-laden ("we worship what we know; salvation is of the Jews," v.22), and the verse says nothing against elements Christ himself instituted *afterward* (the Supper: "this do," Luke 22:19; the Word and prayer: Acts 2:42's "the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers" as the post-Pentecost — most Spirit-filled — church's *structure*; 1 Cor 14:40 "decently and in order" written to the *most* charismatic congregation in the NT). "In spirit" governs the *how* of the elements, not their abolition; dropping Word and sacrament is Q109's "taking from" worship, not ascending past it. Standards' teaching supplied: Q108's element list. Two-sided guard: the holdout must not be armed with "liturgy for liturgy's sake" — the pastor's *diagnosis* (rote formalism is real and dead forms are condemned — Isa 29:13, Matt 15:8–9) is the true element to concede; the *prescription* (remove the elements) is the twist.

- WLC Q109 — "corrupting the worship of God, adding to it, or taking from it"
- WCF 1.9

stem: My church runs a "shepherding covenant" and I signed it gladly two years ago. Lately the applications have escalated: my assigned elder now expects to approve major purchases (he vetoed our car choice), directed me to end a friendship he judges "unedifying," and this month told me which job offer to take "as a matter of submission." When I hesitated he opened to Hebrews 13:17: "**Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls**, as they that must give account." He asked, gently: "Does the verse say 'obey when you agree'? Trust the means God gave you." I can't answer the verse. It really does say obey, and he really is my elder, and he really will give account. So... does faithfulness mean handing him these decisions?
key:
binding-direction TW3 — a real submission text inflated past its scope into a general power of attorney over adiaphora. Refutation from the text's own terms: Heb 13:17's rulers "watch for your **souls**" — the verse defines its own jurisdiction (the ministry of Word, sacrament, discipline: teaching, warning, guarding doctrine and life *against sin*), and the chapter's context (v.7: leaders "who have spoken unto you the word of God"; v.9 warning against "divers and strange doctrines") ties the rule to the Word. Where Scripture is silent (which car, which lawful job, which lawful friendship), the elder's *counsel* may be weighty; his *command* has no warrant — Q127's obedience-clause carries its own limit ("lawful commands"), the Standards' deepest cut is Q105's sin of "making men the lords of our faith and conscience," and WCF 20.2 names conscience-binding "beside" the Word as the violation. The true element to concede in full: real submission to real elders in their real jurisdiction is commanded and countercultural — the answer must not curdle into "no one tells me anything" autonomy (the opposite failure); the covenant-signing is also engaged honestly (a vow to a lawful thing binds in its lawful scope; it cannot have transferred what was never his to receive).

- WLC Q127 — "willing obedience to their lawful commands and counsels" (the scope-word *lawful*)
- WCF 20.2
- WCF 1.9
